question_type: Weighted average (1:2) of total Federal securities at two February month-ends (1980, 1981), in millions, whole number

opus_divergence.what_opus_did: Three tables print a total for Federal securities: FD-1 Summary of Federal Debt, OFS-1 Distribution of Federal Securities, and TSO-1 Summary of Federal Securities in the Treasury Survey of Ownership. Opus chose the FD-1/OFS-1 'Total Federal securities outstanding' series, reading end-of-month rows from the April issues. It gave three reasons: the stub 'End of fiscal year or month' matches 'month-end'; one April 1981 OFS-1 holds both February rows; and FD-1 and OFS-1 agree across every vintage. It rejected TSO-1 because TSO-1 is a sum of rounded components and runs one unit lower. The key follows TSO-1, so Opus's result is off by one unit in the last place.
opus_divergence.what_right_glm_did: The prompt arm took the 'Total Federal securities' row of the Treasury Survey of Ownership dated at each February month-end: TSO-1 in the April 1980 and April 1981 issues. It reached that survey by reasoning that 'reports for the February month-end' means the survey dated Feb 29, 1980 / Feb 28, 1981, printed two months later ([20]-[21]). It confirmed the survey date headers ([28]: 1981_04:4713 'Summary of Federal Securities February 28, 1981'; 1980_04:5382). It also confirmed the values print only once ([32]). It never read the OFS-1/FD-1 February rows. The OFS-1 header line appeared in its [22] grep output, but it did not follow up.
opus_divergence.evidence: Opus: worklog.md:15 (the ambiguity is noted up front), worklog.md:43-48 (TSO-1 alternative), worklog.md:61-68 (source choice and reasons), solution.json decisions[0]. GLM prompt: [1] (first hypothesis already 'Treasury Survey of Ownership'), [20]-[22], [25], [28]-[35].

reviewer_flag: Verdict UNCERTAIN: 'a genuine 1-unit table ambiguity'. The reviewer noted that the question wording has hooks for TSO-1, since 'federal securities values' and 'reports for the February month-end' echo the TSO-1 title 'Summary of Federal Securities February 28, 1981'. It found 'no decisive evidence either way' and kept Opus's answer by default. It also corrected a small arithmetic slip in the worklog about component sums. This is the only one of the four questions where the reviewer flagged the right alternative.
right_by_principled_choice_or_luck: Partly principled, partly luck. The choice was primed by adapter text. The prompt AGENTS.md carries a verified lesson L-tso-survey-tables (conventions around line 140; lesson around lines 574-580): 'the survey dated end of month M prints ONCE, in the M+2 bulletin'. The arm's first THINK already guessed the Treasury Survey of Ownership, and it applied the M+2 cadence correctly at [20]-[21], although it did not cite the lesson id. It also matched the question's 'federal securities ... reports for the February month-end' to a survey table titled with the February month-end date. But it never adjudicated against OFS-1/FD-1, so it never faced the tie that Opus and the reviewer could not break.
wrong_glm_arms_same_as_opus: Cards: yes. It picked OFS-1 'Total Federal securities outstanding' from the April issues and scanned later reprints for revisions ([25]-[37]), the same as Opus, and got Opus's answer. The cards deck had no relevant card; its [27] says C003 does not match. None: no. It used the same TSO-1 row family as the right prompt arm and took the 1981 endpoint correctly from the April 1981 issue. For 1980, though, it took the March 1980 issue's survey, which is dated January 31 ([30]: 'Feb 1980 value likely March 1980 TSO-1 Feb 28 1980'). The correct 1980_04:5374 row was already in its [25] grep output. This is a DATE_OR_PERIOD slip (cadence applied to one endpoint only), about 1% off, and unrelated to Opus's choice.
lesson_for_harness: When several tables print the 'same' total and differ only by rounding, the key followed the table whose title, date stamp and row label best match the question's wording: a survey titled 'Summary of Federal Securities <February month-end date>' with a 'Total Federal securities' row. The headline series with the matching stub did not win. Opus's tie-breakers (stub wording, stability across vintages, agreement between two tables) are sensible, but the benchmark apparently authored from the TSO page. Harness implications: (1) TOOL: a candidate-enumeration lookup that, given a row label, lists every table in the relevant issues carrying it, with title, date stamp and caption, so the tie is visible. (2) TEXT/STATE: a tie-break convention, 'prefer the table whose title/date stamp lexically matches the question; a dated survey matches a phrase like reports for the <month>-end'. (3) STATE: a per-table-family memory like L-tso-survey-tables, which is what steered the one correct arm. For the none arm, a CHECK that both endpoints come from the same table family with the same date-to-issue cadence would have caught the January/February mismatch.
notes: An exact-match grader turns a 1-unit table ambiguity into a hard fail, so which table to use is the whole question here. The prompt arm's AGENTS.md was about 74 KB; its useful content was one table-family lesson. Nothing in the lesson says 'prefer TSO over OFS-1'; it only made the survey the first hypothesis. Opus's worklog also records that the phrase 'Total U.S. Federal Securities' appears nowhere in the corpus, so the question paraphrases a table label, and both candidate labels are equally close. Operational friction was the same in all arms (rg blocked, heredoc failure, python shim problems in none [8]-[10]) and did not matter.
